title: Environment IAM Concordance and Evidence Automation Notes
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a pragmatic concordance (mapping) of IAM roles and responsibilities across Redwood’s three deployment footprints (hosted, dedicated, private), plus an evidence-automation sketch for audit ingestion and SIEM export. Goal: provide security engineers, SREs, and product owners with a single-page reference and a runnable checklist for shipping role changes and ensuring evidentiary telemetry is available for audits.

High-level approach:
- Define a small set of orthogonal role families (Administrative, Tenant Ops, Service, Support, Audit) and map these to environment-specific constraints.
- Provide concise policy templates for common operations (model deploy, config change, tenant data access).
- Specify the audit-log schema and recommended Elastic/Common Event Schema (ECS)-aligned field mapping for SIEM export.
- Outline an evidence-automation runbook that ties IAM changes to generated artifacts (git commits, approval tickets, ephemeral creds, attestation records).

Role families (conceptual):
- Administrative: global controls, platform-level config (example: PlatformAdmin). Strongly scoped in private deployments.
- Tenant Ops: tenant-scoped management (tenant creation, billing metadata, per-tenant model pinning). Examples: TenantAdmin, TenantViewer.
- Service: machine/service principals used by workloads (model-runner, cache-updater).
- Support: human support roles with read-only or time-limited escalation (SupportReadOnly, SupportEscalateTemp).
- Audit/Ingestor: dedicated principal(s) that own log export and SIEM ingest pipelines (AuditWriter, SIEMConnector).

Environment concordance matrix (reader-friendly):
- Hosted:
  - PlatformAdmin: limited to infra ops team; needs 2FA + VIP approval for permanent grants.
  - TenantAdmin: delegated to customer-agent accounts or internal tenant-operational identities. TenantAdmin cannot change platform-wide quotas.
  - Service: long-lived service accounts for internal subsystems; secrets stored in secrets manager with rotation policy 30d.
  - SupportReadOnly: read-only across tenant metadata, cannot access tenant content.
  - AuditWriter: write-only to logging topic; SIEMConnector pulls from audit topic via ephemeral credentials.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity):
  - PlatformAdmin: broader than hosted (capacity config), but must be scoped to the customer-reserved cluster. Use resource-scoped roles (cluster:<customer-id>:PlatformAdmin).
  - TenantAdmin: similar to hosted but may include additional controls for quota management.
  - Service: where customer-managed integrations exist, use customer-scoped service accounts with constrained network egress.
  - SupportReadOnly: for enterprise customers, require explicit customer opt-in and audit attestation.
  - AuditWriter: logs exported to customer-provided SIEM endpoint or to Redwood-managed retention depending on contract.

- Private (VPC/on-prem):
  - PlatformAdmin: ideally not present in Redwood-managed control plane; use customer-local administrators. Where Redwood needs access, use short-lived cross-account/SSH bastion access with recorded approval.
  - TenantAdmin: fully customer-controlled. Redwood provides templates that the customer applies.
  - Service: often embedded in on-prem orchestrator; encourage local KMS/HSM-bound service principals.
  - SupportReadOnly: no default cross-tenant support; escalation requires recorded attestation and per-case approval.
  - AuditWriter: must follow customer retention and export policy; Redwood’s connector runs in-customer network.

Sample role-to-permission mapping (short):
- PlatformAdmin -> {org:read, org:write, infra:manage, billing:read} (production ban on direct data access)
- TenantAdmin -> {tenant:read, tenant:write, model:pin, model:deploy (limited)}
- TenantViewer -> {tenant:read, logs:read (metadata only)}
- Service/model-runner -> {model:execute, kvcache:read, metrics:emit} with no logs:read of tenant content by default
- SupportReadOnly -> {tenant:read(metadata), logs:read(operational), escalate:request} ephemeral escalate flow requires approval ticket

Policy template (human-readable snippet; canonical JSON policy blob to live in infra repo):
- Name: "tenant-model-deploy-policy"
- Principals: TenantAdmin or service account with deploy tag
- Actions allowed: model:deploy, model:rollback (only when a signed runbook present), model:pin
- Constraints: resource.tenant == principal.tenant OR principal.has(org:platform-admin)

Example policy JSON (paste as text, not executed here):
"{\n  \"version\": \"1\",\n  \"statement\": [\n    {\n      \"effect\": \"allow\",\n      \"principal\": {\n        \"role\": [\"tenant-admin\", \"service-deployer\"]\n      },\n      \"action\": [\"model:deploy\", \"model:pin\"],\n      \"resource\": \"arn:redwood:tenant:${tenant_id}:model/*\",\n      \"condition\": {\n        \"StringEquals\": {\n          \"principal:tenant_id\": \"${tenant_id}\"\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}\n"

Audit log schema (recommended fields for every IAM decision/event):
- event.timestamp (ISO8601)
- event.id (uuid)
- event.type (iam.decision | auth.token.issue | policy.change | role.assignment | service.credential.rotate)
- actor.id (user/service principal id)
- actor.type (user | service | system)
- actor.role_labels (comma-separated role names)
- tenant.id (nullable for platform events)
- resource.arn (standardized resource identifier)
- action (string: e.g., model:deploy)
- decision (allow | deny | challenge)
- policy.version (policy id or git commit)
- request.id (correlation id)
- client.ip (ip or cidr range)
- outcome.reason (free text short code for deny)

SIEM export mapping (ECS-friendly) recommendation:
- timestamp -> @timestamp
- event.id -> event.id
- event.type -> event.category / event.action mapping where category = "iam" and action = event.type
- actor.id -> user.id (if human) or process.pid/service.account -> process.executing_user
- tenant.id -> labels.tenant_id or host.metadata.tenant_id
- resource.arn -> url.path or related.resource
- decision -> event.outcome
- request.id -> trace.id or event.id

Notes on PII and minimization: do not include full request payload or tenant data in logs. Mask any identifiers tied to user content. Audit log must explicitly mark whether content was accessed vs control-plane-only.

Evidence automation runbook (high level):
1) On role assignment/change (git-backed policy change preferred):
   - Create PR in infra/policies with policy diff (automatically generated).
   - Require 2 approvers from security and platform.
   - On merge, CI triggers a policy deployment job that records a signed deployment artifact (artifact id, commit sha, deploy timestamp).
   - Emit event.type=policy.change with policy.version set to commit sha and attach links to PR/Ticket in event.metadata.link (short id).
2) On privileged escalation (temporary):
   - Create escalation request ticket (Jira) with TTL and justification.
   - Create ephemeral credential via STS (duration limited) and record STS issuance event (event.type=auth.token.issue) including request.id and ttl.
   - Automatically schedule a verification snapshot at TTL-30m that re-checks whether the credential is still in use; emit evidence artifact.
3) On role removal / deprovision:
   - Run a scavenger job to find orphaned service principals or issued tokens; produce a report with remediation actions.
   - Emit event.type=role.deprovision with list of affected resource ARNs (summarized) and ticket link.

Operational checklist for shipping role changes: (short running checklist)
- [ ] Policy authored in infra repo and linted
- [ ] PR created with required reviewers mapped (security + owning product)
- [ ] CI generates policy change event and creates signed artifact
- [ ] SIEMConnector mapping validated in staging (sample payloads present)
- [ ] Evidence automation pipeline recorded the policy.change event and linked PR/Ticket
- [ ] Retention policy verified (hosted: 1y default, dedicated: tied to contract, private: customer-specified)

Testing and validation guidance:
- Use synthetic tenant + replay harness to generate representative model:deploy events and validate that SIEM receives ECS-mapped fields.
- Run red-team style tests that attempt privilege escalation; ensure deny events produce denial audit messages and generate automated alerts to secops.
- Validate that private deployments produce only metadata-level telemetry back to Redwood unless explicitly configured otherwise.

Example SIEM export sample (log event as text line):
"@timestamp:2024-12-03T18:22:31Z event.id=8f3e2b3c actor.id=svc-model-runner-23 actor.type=service actor.role_labels=model-runner,cache-reader tenant.id=tenant-842 resource.arn=arn:redwood:tenant:tenant-842:model:speech-v2 action=model:execute decision=allow policy.version=aa1b2c request.id=trace-993 client.ip=10.0.4.5"

Privacy & contract constraints:
- Hosted: redact tenant content fields; record only metadata+decision.
- Dedicated: support customers may opt-in to broader telemetry; must be captured in contract SOW.
- Private: telemetry must follow customer's network and retention rules; Redwood must provide a deployment checklist that captures what telemetry will leave the environment (if any).

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- Author canonical policy JSON templates for infra repo (TODO: Diego).
- Add SIEMConnector config examples for Splunk/Elastic/Datadog (Priya).
- Ship a lightweight test harness that emits canonical IAM events for end-to-end validation (Samir).

Appendix: quick reference commands and ticket templates (examples you can copy):
- PR title: [policy] tenant-model-deploy: allow model:deploy for tenant-admins
- Jira template short title: Escalation request - temporary support access - tenant-<id>
- Evidence tag conventions: evidence:type=policy.change evidence:artifact=infra-policies@<sha>

End of note.
